plans.name: On-demand list (via sales onboarding)
plans.note: On-demand node prices are public on coreweave.com/pricing, but every CTA on the page is "Contact sales": account access is sales-gated. fee 0 = no platform fee; kept flagged sales so it is opt-in.

caveats: Current node tables bundle CPU/RAM. Do not reuse obsolete per-resource A100 prices. Spot rates are regional point-in-time quotes. Multi-GPU node minimum makes divided rate unsuitable for a single-GPU sandbox.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

2026-09-28: 8-GPU node regimes now priced at list (node price / 8 per GPU, gpu_min_count 8, plan_limits_exempt); alt removed. H100 is only sold as an 8x HGX node ($49.24/h). Access is via sales (plan flagged sales).

Single-GPU prices on coreweave.com/pricing (B200 $8.60, H200 $6.31, H100 $6.16, A100 $2.70, RTX PRO 6000 $2.50, L40S $2.25, L40 $1.25 per GPU-h) apply exclusively to CoreWeave inference-platform customers via an account executive; general compute is sold as 8-GPU nodes.

fleet.notes: Capacity plans are contracted/reserved through account teams, with Flex preview access via account teams. No verified public self-serve new-account VM/GPU default. Contract capacity must not be treated as an instant new-account entitlement.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Save results or checkpoints outside the sandbox before its lifetime expires.
snapshot_auto.note: CoreWeave Sandboxes: lifetime expiry terminates the sandbox without saving; snapshot-on-stop exists but is an explicit opt-in flag on the stop call (StopSandbox fileSystemSnapshotOnStop=true / sandbox.stop(snapshot_on_stop=True)); the first-party cws-agent CLI's `stop` snapshots the workspace by default (client-side default, still a user call). CKS GPU nodes: no machine snapshots. Scheduled, not stop-triggered: Distributed File Storage volumes get a `.snapshot` folder, 'Snapshots ... occur every 6 hours and persist for 72 hours'.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A mid-life snapshot captures a running sandbox without stopping it. The sandbox keeps running afterward.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Sandboxes only (public preview). File System Snapshots: tarball of one chosen working-directory mount (EmptyDir scratch) to object storage (CoreWeave-managed or bring-your-own bucket); filesystem only, no memory/processes, not the whole root FS. New sandboxes can restore it and 'fork one snapshot into several sandboxes'. Also snapshot-on-stop. CKS PVCs can use Kubernetes VolumeSnapshots.

harness_api.quote: cws-agent session start project1 fix-auth --prompt "Fix the login bug"
harness_api.note: First-party (coreweave GitHub org, Apache 2.0) CLI cws-agent: `cws-agent AGENT [NAME]` launches claude, codex, devin, opencode or cursor in a sandbox; starts parallel agent sessions with a prompt (git worktree per task), attach/diff, `cws-agent resume` lists/resumes conversations across running and saved workspaces, `cws-agent run api1 "task"` for OpenAI Agents API workers, Telegram/Discord chat bridges. CLI only (no documented REST/SDK harness endpoint or event stream API); docs also list integrations for Claude Managed Agents, OpenAI Agents API, Devin Outposts, Pi, Muse Code.

egress_allowlist.quote: An HTTPS hostname, exact or with a single leftmost wildcard label, such as `*.example.com`.
egress_allowlist.note: Sandboxes: EgressRule = cidr (with except carve-outs) | https_hostname (TCP 443 only) | tenant | selector | any, with ports; allow-only over default-deny, deny_egress flag, runner-policy allowed_egress/default_egress, DNS egress mode. Enforced by the runner/platform, not in the sandbox. CKS: Kubernetes/Cilium network policies (toCIDR; toFQDN needs a support ticket to enable Cilium's L7 DNS proxy).

egress_http_rules.quote: Hostname rules authorize HTTPS access, not DNS queries.
egress_http_rules.note: Sandbox EgressRule schema only has cidr / https_hostname / tenant / any / selector / ports; no method/path/header matching. Cilium L7 HTTP policies on CKS not documented.

ingress_rules.quote: `egress` and `ingress` are allow-only rule sets over default-deny
ingress_rules.note: Sandboxes: choose which ports get a public endpoint (a service without `endpoint` gets no public address); IngressRule CIDR allowlists for CUSTOM-visibility ports; runner policy allowed_ingress/default_ingress; deny_ingress. Public endpoints themselves are auth=OPEN only ('The platform does not authenticate callers'); auth=TOKEN returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED. CKS: network policies, LoadBalancer services, VPCs.

secret_proxy.quote: it resolves the values from your W&B team and injects them as environment variables
secret_proxy.note: W&B Secret Manager secrets are injected as env vars (serverless only); CKS uses Kubernetes Secrets. No credential-injecting egress proxy documented.

volume_attach.quote: Registered Volumes are volumes your organization registers once, and any number of sandboxes can then mount them.
volume_attach.note: Sandboxes: scratch volumes (die with the sandbox) and Registered Volumes backed by an existing PVC in your CKS cluster (persistent, independent lifecycle). CKS: PVCs on Distributed File Storage (VAST) and local storage.

volume_shared.quote: Use a registered Volume for data that outlives a sandbox or that several sandboxes read at once
volume_shared.note: Read-write by default, read_only per mount or per Volume. Registered Volumes are CKS-backed PVCs (cluster placement). Distributed File Storage PVCs use accessMode ReadWriteMany, only within the cluster where deployed.

isolation.quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) offers a managed Kubernetes service that lets you run clusters on bare metal servers ... clusters use Data Processing Unit (DPU) technology to provide enhanced isolation ... Each CKS cluster operates within its own private Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).
isolation.note: GPU/CPU compute nodes and sandboxes are Kubernetes Pods scheduled on bare-metal Nodes; tenant isolation is via VPC/DPU network segmentation, not a per-tenant hypervisor VM.

image_oci.note: Sandboxes and CKS workloads start from a customer-specified container/OCI image.

docker_inside.quote: Enable Docker-in-Docker inside SUNK clusters by configuring AppArmor, privileged pods, and s6 services
docker_inside.note: Documented for SUNK (Slurm-on-CoreWeave); Sandboxes also support multi-container 'Docker Compose file' sandboxes (create-from-file).

nested_virt.quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service ... managed Kubernetes on bare metal
nested_virt.note: not offered: no CoreWeave documentation exposes /dev/kvm or nested virtualization inside CKS Pods or Sandboxes; the platform's own virtualization boundary (DPU/VPC) is at the Node level, not the guest.

desktop.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. GPU instances can be used to build VDI workloads, but CoreWeave does not ship a managed desktop/VNC/RDP product.

browser.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no managed/preinstalled browser product documented.

computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no browser-stealth/fingerprinting feature documented.

captcha_solving.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Outbound traffic from your Pods leaves the cluster through a NAT that uses a stable, documented set of public IP ranges per Availability Zone.
egress_ip_type.note: Ranges are fixed/documented per-AZ but shared across tenants in that AZ, not a dedicated IP per customer.

ssh.quote: Use this for plain TCP workloads such as SSH ... The following sample manifest defines a LoadBalancer Service that exposes an sshd Pod on port 22
ssh.note: Also documented for SUNK Slurm login/compute Nodes ("Connect to the Slurm login node ... using SSH").

snapshot.quote: A mid-life snapshot captures a running sandbox without stopping it ... filesystem only, no memory/processes
snapshot.note: Filesystem-only snapshots (Sandboxes File System Snapshots, CKS Kubernetes VolumeSnapshots on PVCs); no whole-machine memory snapshot.

fork.quote: New sandboxes can restore it and 'fork one snapshot into several sandboxes'
fork.note: Fork is via a filesystem snapshot restored into new sandboxes.

fork_running.quote: A mid-life snapshot captures a running sandbox without stopping it. The sandbox keeps running afterward.
fork_running.note: The source sandbox keeps running while its snapshot is forked into new sandboxes; the new sandboxes are freshly restored, not a live in-place clone.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: filesystem only, no memory/processes, not the whole root FS
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Forked sandboxes start fresh from a filesystem snapshot; running processes are not carried over.

pause_resume.quote: The platform terminates it when the lifetime expires ... A workload that finishes or a sandbox that you stop can end sooner.
pause_resume.note: not offered: sandboxes/CKS Nodes are stopped/deleted and billed for reserved capacity, not paused/resumed with reduced billing.

wake_on_request.quote: Set the lifetime when you create the sandbox to give an agent, development environment, or batch workload enough time to finish.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: no documentation of a stopped/sleeping machine auto-waking on an inbound request.

persistent_disk.quote: Use a registered Volume for data that outlives a sandbox or that several sandboxes read at once
persistent_disk.note: Node/sandbox-local (scratch/Local Storage) storage is ephemeral, but attached persistent volumes (Registered Volumes, Distributed File Storage, Object Storage PVCs) survive stop/start.

live_resize.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
live_resize.note: not offered: no documentation of changing a running Node's/sandbox's CPU/RAM/GPU allocation without recreating it.

agent_harnesses.quote: cws-agent session start project1 fix-auth --prompt "Fix the login bug"
agent_harnesses.note: First-party cws-agent CLI launches Claude Code, Codex, Devin, OpenCode, or Cursor inside a sandbox.

own_agent_api.quote: CoreWeave Mission Control Agent is now available in public preview ... Ask operational questions in plain language and review answers with supporting evidence.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: Mission Control Agent is a first-party infrastructure-operations agent (querying/managing CoreWeave resources), not a browser/computer-use/research task agent as defined.

mcp_server.quote: CoreWeave Mission Control MCP is now generally available. It lets you access CoreWeave operational tools from Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible clients such as Claude Code, Cursor, and the ChatGPT desktop app.
mcp_server.note: Mission Control MCP exposes CoreWeave platform/observability tools (and gated write tools that can modify resources) via MCP; it is a platform-ops server rather than a sandbox-lifecycle-specific one.

lang_python.quote: Create an environment, run commands, work with files, and collect results through the Python or TypeScript software development kit (SDK).

lang_node.quote: explore the Python client and TypeScript SDK

public_ipv4.quote: CoreWeave supports both Public IPv4 addresses and Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP)

inbound_https.quote: HTTPS: The platform terminates TLS at its edge with a certificate it provisions and renews, then forwards the request to your port as cleartext HTTP.
inbound_https.note: Also available on CKS via LoadBalancer Services + Traefik Ingress with cert-manager-issued TLS.

guest_firewall.quote: clusters use Data Processing Unit (DPU) technology to provide enhanced isolation and performance
guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is container (CKS Pods on bare metal), not a full VM/microVM, and network policy enforcement is offloaded to the DPU/Cilium at the platform level rather than guaranteed nftables/iptables control inside the guest.

static_egress_ip.quote: Outbound traffic from your Pods leaves the cluster through a NAT that uses a stable, documented set of public IP ranges per Availability Zone.
static_egress_ip.note: Fixed, allowlistable per-AZ NAT ranges rather than a single dedicated IP per tenant.

windows.quote: About GPU instances ... Compare CoreWeave GPU instance types
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; all documented GPU/CPU instance and sandbox images are Linux-based.

macos.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; CoreWeave is a bare-metal/Linux GPU cloud with no macOS offering.

arm64.quote: CoreWeave's GB300 NVL72-powered cloud instances ... Each rack includes 72 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs, 36 NVIDIA Grace CPUs (Arm-based), and 18 NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPUs
arm64.note: GB200/GB300 NVL72 and GH200 instances use NVIDIA Grace (Arm) host CPUs.

self_host.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; CoreWeave is a hosted cloud provider, not software you run on your own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; workloads run in CoreWeave's own data centers, not deployed into a customer-owned cloud account.

open_source.quote: GPU Cloud ... on-demand and reserved GPU compute for AI training and inference
open_source.note: not offered: the core CoreWeave platform is proprietary; only ancillary tools such as the cws-agent CLI (Apache 2.0) are open source.

soc2.note: CoreWeave's own Trust Center (Conveyor-hosted) lists SOC 2 Type II among its certifications.

hipaa.note: CoreWeave's Trust Center certifications list does not include HIPAA/HIPAA-CE, and no HIPAA/BAA page was found on coreweave.com or docs.coreweave.com.

sso.quote: Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Single Sign-On (SSO) together form an authentication method for CoreWeave Cloud. Users in your organization authenticate through the same identity provider (IdP)

eu_data_residency.note: CoreWeave offers EU Availability Zones (e.g. EU-SOUTH-03B/04A) where GPU/CPU instances and data can be placed.

max_session_h.note: GPU/CPU compute Nodes are billed per node-hour and run until the customer stops them; no documented forced maximum session length. (The separate CoreWeave Sandboxes serverless/CKS product caps sandbox lifetime at 30 days / 720h.)
